deep.reconstruction:
Context (from the previous page and the bundle title): this belongs to Riemann's study of electrostatic equilibrium on parallel circular cylinders. The plane cross-section is a domain bounded by circles with centres p, p1, p2, ... and radii r, r1, r2, ... It is mapped conformally (x+yi = f(xi+eta i), marginal note) onto a half-plane in an auxiliary variable zeta (the script 'z'/'Z' of the manuscript, called zeta here), with cuts K1, K2. The previous page counts sheets: each zeta in the upper half-plane corresponds to three values of z.

Heading: 'Ausdruck von zeta durch z zu finden' (find the expression connecting zeta and z).

(1) Reflection principle. Riemann writes the correspondence (his sign ‡) zeta ‡ zeta' || (z-p)/r ‡ r/(z'-p'), where a prime denotes the complex conjugate. Read in modern terms: when zeta is replaced by its mirror image conj(zeta) across the real axis, z is replaced by its inversion in the boundary circle |z-p| = r, namely z* = p + r^2/(conj(z) - conj(p)). Equivalently, (z*-p)/r = r/(conj z - conj p). The same is begun for the circle (p1, r1): (z-p1)/r1 ‡ [r1/(z'-p1'), left unfinished].

(2) Conclusion, stated in words. When zeta returns to the same value through an even number of reflections, z undergoes a composition of an even number of circle inversions. Such a composition is a Möbius map. 'The different values which z can take while zeta takes the same value again are thus rational functions of first degree of one of these values.' Riemann first wrote 'algebraische' and corrected it to 'rationale'. So the branches satisfy z -> (az+b)/(cz+d).

(3) Derivative. Under z -> (az+b)/(cz+d), the derivative transforms as dz/dzeta -> (ad-bc)/(cz+d)^2 * dz/dzeta (chain rule).

(4) Linearization. Set y = 1/sqrt(dz/dzeta) and y1 = z/sqrt(dz/dzeta). Then:
- y -> (cz+d)/sqrt(ad-bc) * y = (c*y1 + d*y)/sqrt(ad-bc);
- y1 -> (az+b)/(cz+d) * (cz+d)/sqrt(ad-bc) * y = (a*y1 + b*y)/sqrt(ad-bc).
So the pair (y, y1) transforms by a linear substitution of determinant 1, up to sign. This is exactly what is written in the two last lines.

Next page (continuation, for orientation):
- The Wronskian is y*y1' - y1*y' = 1 (since y1/y = z and (y1/y)' = z' = 1/y^2).
- Differentiating gives y*y1'' - y1*y'' = 0, so y''/y = y1''/y1.
- This common quotient is invariant under the substitutions, hence a single-valued function of zeta.
- In modern terms y''/y = -(1/2){z, zeta}, the Schwarzian derivative. So z is a ratio of two solutions of y'' = Q(zeta) y with Q single-valued.

This is the uniformization / Schwarzian-ODE method for circle domains (Schottky-type groups), which will determine the mapping function.
errors: No mathematical errors in what is written. The first correspondence for circle p is complete. The analogous one for circle p1 is left unfinished (r1/(z'-p1') missing).

A single reflection gives an anti-holomorphic map, not a Möbius map. The claim of 'rational functions of first degree' holds for even compositions, i.e. when zeta really returns to the same value, not its conjugate. Riemann's wording is consistent with this but leaves it implicit.
The square roots carry a sign ambiguity: the substitutions on (y, y1) are determined only up to ±1. Riemann does not comment, and it is harmless for the invariance of y''/y.
The derivative written ∂z/∂zeta on both sides must be read as: the derivative of the transformed branch equals (ad-bc)/(cz+d)^2 times the old derivative. The notation is compressed but correct.

results.what: Boundary circles correspond to the real zeta-axis; continuation across a circle is inversion in that circle (z* = p + r^2/(conj z - conj p)).
results.modern_name: Schwarz reflection principle for circular arcs
results.usually_credited_to: H. A. Schwarz (1869-70); Riemann used reflection ideas in his Nachlass

results.what: Branches of the inverse map z(zeta) are related by Möbius transformations (compositions of even numbers of circle inversions).
results.modern_name: Monodromy group of a circle domain / Schottky group
results.usually_credited_to: F. Schottky (1877); Riemann's posthumous paper on cylinders with circular cross-section (Werke, 1876) is known to anticipate it

results.what: y = (z')^{-1/2} and y1 = z (z')^{-1/2} transform linearly with determinant 1 under Möbius changes of z; their Wronskian is 1; y''/y = y1''/y1 is invariant, i.e. the Schwarzian derivative.
results.modern_name: Linearization of the Schwarzian derivative: z as a ratio of solutions of y'' = Q y
results.usually_credited_to: Kummer (1836) / Schwarz (1869-73); named by Cayley (1880). Riemann used it in the hypergeometric and minimal-surface Nachlass

deep.surprise_reason: The material matches Riemann's posthumously published paper on electric equilibrium on cylinders with circular cross-section (Werke, ed. Weber), which is already recognized as anticipating Schottky groups and the Schwarzian-ODE method. Riemann's use of the Schwarzian-type invariant is also documented elsewhere. This page is a draft of known work, though a nice explicit record of the y, y1 linearization.

checkable.asserts: 1/sqrt(z') transforms to (c*y1 + d*y)/sqrt(ad-bc), with w = dz/dzeta (should be 0 for positive branch).

transcription_corrections: The symbol rendered '‡' is Riemann's correspondence sign ('goes over into / corresponds to'), not a mathematical operator.
The primes in z', p' denote complex conjugates (mirror values), not derivatives.

The variable rendered zeta is written as a script/Fraktur z in the image, and the next page renders it 'g'. Both stand for the same auxiliary variable; the heading's second letter looks like a capital Z, matching the Z of the previous page.
Second correspondence line is incomplete: '(z-p1)/r1 ‡' with nothing after it.
In the struck-out item before the final formulas, the image shows a crossed-out partial expression (apparently a start of a sqrt of dz/dzeta), not clearly '\sqrt{z}'.
